sentences.text: Never leave the dock without the marine forecast.
The National Weather Service issues coastal and offshore forecasts, online and on NOAA Weather Radio.
And learn what the warnings mean, because the exam asks for the numbers.
A small craft advisory: winds of roughly twenty to thirty-three knots, or hazardous seas.
The exact threshold varies by region.
A gale warning: thirty-four to forty-seven knots.
A storm warning: forty-eight to sixty-three knots.
A hurricane force wind warning: sixty-four knots and over.
And a special marine warning, for short-lived hazards: severe thunderstorms, waterspouts, sudden strong gusts.
That last one can be issued with minutes of notice.
So the numbers to hold on to are thirty-four, forty-eight and sixty-four.
